title: Thanthai Periyar and the Vaikom Satyagraha: Breaking the Shackles of Caste Segregation (1924)
summary: In 1924, when local leaders were arrested during the Vaikom temple road entry movement, Periyar E. V. Ramasamy led the protest to historic victory, earning the title 'Vaikom Veerar'.
full_text:
In April 1924, the temple town of Vaikom in the princely state of Travancore (modern Kerala) was the battleground for one of modern India's most momentous human rights struggles.

The orthodoxy of the day strictly barred lower-caste Ezhavas, Pulayas, and other marginalized communities from even walking on the public streets surrounding the prominent Mahadeva temple. When local organizers initiated a peaceful satyagraha, the state authorities swiftly arrested every prominent Kerala leader, threatening to crush the movement entirely.

Desperate for leadership, the organizers sent an urgent telegraph to Tamil Nadu: "Leaders arrested. Movement in peril. Pray come immediately."

Periyar E. V. Ramasamy, then President of the Tamil Nadu Congress Committee, departed for Vaikom without delay. Arriving in Travancore, he mobilized the local populace, organized picketing campaigns, and enlisted his wife Nagammal and sister Kannammal to lead women’s demonstrations.

When the colonial Resident and princely police warned Periyar that as an outsider he faced severe hard labor, Periyar replied with fearless moral defiance:
"Human dignity knows no regional boundaries! When cows, dogs, and horses are permitted to walk freely upon public roads maintained by taxpayer funds, by what moral authority can you forbid human beings from walking on them? Until every citizen can walk with head held high along these streets, I shall not leave Travancore, nor will prison walls extinguish our resolve!"

Periyar was arrested twice and subjected to grueling prison conditions. The sustained moral pressure ultimately forced the Travancore regency to throw open the temple roads to all communities. Periyar returned to Tamil Nadu hailed forever as 'Vaikom Veerar'—the Hero of Vaikom.
